load_bearing_verifications.claim: The sole direct PubMed clomiphene-plus-gout hit studied participants with pre-existing gout and did not test incident gout or clomiphene-induced hyperuricemia.
Testosterone exposure increased serum urate in the adjacent 160-person human cohort used for mechanistic plausibility.

In the prospective 69-person cross-sex hormone cohort, mean serum urate in the 47-person transmasculine group rose from 3.91 mg/dL at baseline to 5.07 at one year and remained 5.02 at two years; mean fractional excretion of urate in a 25-person subgroup fell from 8.78% to 6.93% at two years (P = 0.004).
The official US Clomid label does not contain gout, hyperuricemia, or increased uric acid as a recognized event.
Accessible male clomiphene safety publications did not report serum urate or incident gout as tracked endpoints.
All three clomiphene-gout openFDA co-reports coded clomiphene as concomitant and lacked usable exposure-to-onset chronology.
Dual-energy CT has documented silent monosodium urate deposition in asymptomatic hyperuricemia.
The disclosed n=1 chronology and laboratory values reproduce the source record while distinguishing first documented podagra, mixed urate measurement systems, and an unconfirmed joint prominence.
load_bearing_verifications.primary_source: Disclosed project-lead longitudinal source record; underlying files private

limitations: No prospective clomiphene study located measured serum urate, incident gout, or renal/intestinal urate handling.
Regional result pages were reached but not all yielded machine-parseable counts or complete relevance sets.
No non-English source supplied a load-bearing claim, so the two-model translation protocol was not triggered.
Spontaneous adverse-event co-reports cannot establish causality or incidence.
The hypothesis-generating longitudinal record lacks pre-initiation urate, paired same-assay dechallenge measurements, imaging confirmation, and confounder control.
